title: Dinosaurs Were Reptiles
objective: After this level you can explain what dinosaurs were and how we know about them.
summary: Dinosaurs were reptiles, named by Owen in 1842. They stood on pillar-like legs; pterosaurs and sea reptiles were not dinosaurs. Maiasaura's nests show eggs laid on land.

cards.headline: The first dinosaur was named mostly from a jawbone.
cards.body: In 1824, William Buckland described Megalosaurus from fossils made up mainly of a lower jawbone with a few teeth. Nobody yet had a word for the kind of animal it was. So what were these creatures, and how can we tell?

cards.headline: Terrible reptiles
cards.body: In 1842, Richard Owen studied the remains of three giant extinct animals and proposed a new group: Dinosauria. He built the name from Greek deinos, 'terrible' or 'fearfully great', and sauros, 'reptile' or 'lizard'. The reptile part was right. Dinosaurs were a diverse group of reptiles, in the same class as the turtles, lizards and crocodilians earlier in this chapter. Don't let 'lizard' fool you, though. Look at the legs.

cards.headline: Legs like pillars
cards.body: What set dinosaurs apart was how they stood. They held their legs straight under the body like columns, the way elephants do, instead of sprawled out to the sides like a lizard's. Their hip sockets even had a hole right through. Flying pterosaurs and sea reptiles like plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs were reptiles too, but on separate branches. Reptiles, yes. Dinosaurs, no.

mascot.line: Pterosaurs and plesiosaurs get called dinosaurs all the time. Check the legs.

cards.fact: One dinosaur left a whole nesting ground.
cards.context: In 1978, a nesting site turned up near Choteau, Montana: nests with clutches of eggs, broken eggshells and baby dinosaurs. The babies were too young to walk, yet their teeth were worn, so someone was feeding them. Jack Horner and Bob Makela named the animal Maiasaura, 'good mother lizard'. Eggs in nests on land: the reptile plan from Level 31, preserved in stone.

cards.headline: Dinosaurs: explained
learned: Dinosaurs were a diverse group of reptiles
Legs held under the body like pillars
Pterosaurs and plesiosaurs: reptiles, not dinosaurs
Maiasaura's 1978 nests: eggs laid on land

questions.prompt: In Owen's word Dinosauria, the Greek 'sauros' means _____.

options.label: great in size
options.rationale: Close to deinos's 'fearfully great', not sauros.

questions.explanation: Owen joined deinos ('terrible' or 'fearfully great') with sauros ('reptile' or 'lizard').

questions.prompt: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles. Why aren't they counted as dinosaurs?

options.label: No true reptile has ever been able to fly
They were early mammals with skin wings
They evolved separately, without the dinosaur hip
They laid no eggs, so they can't be reptiles
options.rationale: Eggs aren't the test; the dinosaur branch and hip are.

questions.explanation: Pterosaurs evolved separately from dinosaurs and lack the dinosaur hip socket with a hole through it.

questions.prompt: Put these names in the order they were given, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Buckland described Megalosaurus in 1824, Owen proposed Dinosauria in 1842, and Maiasaura was named after the 1978 nesting ground find.
